body: Our research has applied the three main indicators of STWM to the Arctic region with regard to the Arctic Council states in the period since 2014. We have sought to answer whether the conflict potential has been trending upwards since 2014 and how close it is to a critical threshold based on recent developments. The outcomes show clear evidence confirming rising confrontational behaviour in the militarisation marker. On the other hand,
the rivalry indicator shows continued cooperative behaviour
, while the coalition-building analysis also shows a mostly cooperative approach in the post-Crimea period, then a sharp decline after February 2022.

Thus, the STWM, as one of the most sensitive models of escalation potential of territorial disputes, confirms confrontational behaviour in two indicators, militarisation and coalitionbuilding. The latter, however, changed dramatically after February 2022. Regional Arctic coalitions have suspended most forms of cooperation with Russia, and two of the regional actors, Finland and Sweden, applied for NATO membership in May 2022 with Finland joining in April 2023 and Sweden’s membership awaiting Turkish ratification as of November 2023. The evidence also reveals Russian activities as the catalyst of recent military developments, and that confrontational behaviour in the military dimension pits Russia against the other seven Arctic countries. In this regard, further research as to if and under what conditions the Arctic could be a future sphere of new Russian military activities would be valuable.
